title: Constraints the ZPA Terraform docs and provider code place on individual resources

prose.text: These are provider-side constraints the Terraform docs or code state for individual ZPA resources. Each resource's arguments, enums and defaults are generated from the provider code (`node scripts/kb.mjs surface <resource name>`); these are the constraints the schema does not show.

extranet-dto-needs-extranet-enabled.title: Whether extranet_dto on a server group requires extranet_enabled = true
extranet-dto-needs-extranet-enabled.blocks: knowing whether an extranet_dto set with extranet_enabled false is ignored or rejected
extranet-dto-needs-extranet-enabled.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the legacy reference says extranet connectivity requires extranet_enabled = true at the group level before extranet_dto is applied. The server group doc and resource code treat extranet_enabled and extranet_dto as independent arguments, and extranet_dto is sent whenever the user sets it. On the provider side the schema has no RequiredWith tying extranet_dto to extranet_enabled, so Terraform does not reject extranet_dto with extranet_enabled false; whether the API ignores or rejects it is still open.

pra-enabled-required-for-pra.title: Whether pra_enabled must be true on an App Connector group for PRA segments to route through it
pra-enabled-required-for-pra.blocks: knowing whether a PRA segment works when its connector group has pra_enabled false
pra-enabled-required-for-pra.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the legacy reference says pra_enabled = true is required on the App Connector group before PRA segments can route through it. The provider doc describes the attribute only as whether PRA is enabled on the group. The LSS error-code catalog ties a connector failing to establish a PRA tunnel (AST_MT_SETUP_ERR_PRA_UNAVAILABLE) to checking the group's PRA capability, which supports the dependency. Still open: whether every PRA session through a group with the capability off fails, or only some, since no source states the requirement directly.

tag-group-in-policy-conditions.title: Whether tag group IDs can be referenced in policy rule conditions
tag-group-in-policy-conditions.blocks: knowing whether a tag-based policy condition can be written in Terraform
tag-group-in-policy-conditions.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the legacy reference says tags and tag groups are Early Access and it is unconfirmed whether zpa_tag_group IDs can be used as an object_type in policy conditions. The v1 and v2 access rule object_type validators accept WORKLOAD_TAG_GROUP, and the zpa_workload_tag_group data source doc says it is for that object_type. A workload tag group is a distinct object: the Go SDK reads it from /workloadTagGroup/summary, while zpa_tag_group uses /tagGroup. No validator or provider doc names an object type for zpa_tag_group IDs. Provider side answered: the 16 object_type validators (six v1 lists passed to GetPolicyConditionsSchema, ten inline in the v2, capabilities, credential, portal and browser protection rules) hold no tag group type besides WORKLOAD_TAG_GROUP, and each is a StringInSlice ValidateFunc, so Terraform rejects any other object_type before calling the API. Still open: whether the API accepts zpa_tag_group IDs under some object type.

docs-no-import-but-importer-exists.impact: terraform import is not blocked by the provider for these resources even though the docs say it is unsupported; what the import then produces is separate (the schedule read, for example, never writes the ID: zpa.terraform.resource-fidelity).
